response.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.state_county_province AS st, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Accounts a JOIN Customers c ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.state_county_province), sh AS (SELECT st, cnt, 1.0 * cnt / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM s), av AS (SELECT st, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM sh) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_account_base, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM av WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: A state's 'account base' is the number of rows in Accounts belonging to customers in that state. Customers with NULL state_county_province form one group. States with no accounts do not appear.
Share is the state's account count divided by the total account count. The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-state shares, taken over all state groups including the NULL group.
The output's 'average share' is the mean share of the above-average states. 'How far above' is the mean of (share - average share) over those states.

alternatives.interpretation: States with customers but zero accounts are also counted as groups with an account base of 0. This lowers the average share and adds them to the denominator.
alternatives.sql: WITH s AS (SELECT c.state_county_province AS st, COUNT(a.account_id) AS cnt FROM Customers c LEFT JOIN Accounts a ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.state_county_province), sh AS (SELECT st, cnt, 1.0 * cnt / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM s), av AS (SELECT st, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM sh) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS combined_account_base, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM av WHERE share > avg_share;
